_comment: SMART-BASE, declared as an INSTANTIATED harness — the same rule, and the same warrant, as `smart-trust.config.json` and `who-iris.config.json`. The owner's rule (2026-09-21): 'scan the root of the repo, look for <harness>.config.json as named instances', so `harness-tiles.ts` computes `instantiated` from the presence of this file at the instantiation root. The rule was right and the FACT was wrong: this repository does instantiate smart-base — it holds 2575 files under `library/`, 139 under `fhir-artifact-index/` (including the DAK API sidecars every other smart-* instance's tooling reads), plus `tools/`, `skills/`, `methodologies/` and `processes/`, all declared and all gated here. A repository that holds, declares and gates an instance's content is instantiating it, whatever the absence of this file previously said. Owner, 2026-09-23: 'smart-guideline/base need harness'. WHY smart-ig IS NOT GETTING ONE: it declares no directories and holds five boilerplate files, so a config there would assert an instantiation that is not happening — `smart-ig` is a layering waypoint in the needs chain, not a harness. The distinction is the point of the file: it says what is instantiated HERE, and saying it of something empty would make the navbar's harness tiles a list nobody can trust.
_contentType_comment: `document`. smart-base's content here is the IG's artefact index, its DAK API sidecars, its library and its methodology prose — structured prose and data. There is no Lean and no TeX, so the paper adapter's LaTeX-shaped axes would fire `critical` on prose that never reaches pdflatex, which is the `zkgs` failure this field exists to prevent.
